title: Who can manage a custom URL or TLD category: roles and operational scope

prose.text: Managing a custom category is limited by the admin's role and, for User-Defined categories, by the category's operational scope. {{who-can-manage}}

prose.label: Operational scope.
prose.text: {{scope-availability}} {{scope-kinds}} {{scope-limits}} Whether the API carries the scope is open {{gap:api-scopes-field}}.

who-can-manage.statement: Custom categories can be managed only by super admins, admins with the Custom URL Management role, or admins with the Custom URL Management and Override Existing URLs role.

quotes: Custom categories can only be managed by super admins, admins with the Custom URL Management role, or admins with the Custom URL Management and Override Existing URLs role.

scope-availability.statement: The operational scope option is available for a category only when its URL Super Category is User-Defined. Several scopes can be selected, and with more than one scope OR logic is used to find a match.

quotes: Administrator Operational Scope: Choose the operational scope for this category. This option is only available for categories when the URL Super Category is set to User-Defined.
You can select multiple operational scopes; when there is more than one scope, OR logic is used to find a match.

scope-kinds.statement: Any lets any admin manage, and admin roles then control which admins can manage custom categories. Organization lets admins whose scope is Organization manage. Location Group, Location and Department let admins with one or more of the selected items in their scope manage.

quotes: You can then control which admins are able to manage custom categories through admin roles.
Organization: Admins whose scope is Organization can manage.
Location Group: Admins with one or more of the selected location groups in their scope can manage.
Location: Admins with one or more of the selected locations in their scope can manage.
Department: Admins with one or more of the selected departments in their operational scope can manage.

scope-limits.statement: Admins with an operational scope over location groups that include one or more of the selected locations can also manage the category but cannot change its operational scope. A User-Defined category can be deleted only if the admin's scope matches the category's scope exactly. Operational scopes an admin does not see are not part of that admin's operational scope.

quotes: Admins that have an operational scope over location groups that include one or more of the selected locations can also manage. However, they cannot change the operational scope of the category.
You can only delete a custom category that belongs to the User-Defined super category if your administrator scope matches the scope of the custom category exactly.
If there are any operational scopes that you don't see, they are not part of your administrative operational scope.

scope-examples.statement: The page's examples: an admin whose Location scope includes only San Jose and Bangalore can edit Example Category, and an admin whose department scope is only over Sales can also edit it. An admin with the Location Group scope England (London and Manchester) can edit all of Test Category except its operational scope.

quotes: Admin A, who has a Location scope that only includes San Jose and Bangalore, can edit Example Category. Admin B, whose department scope is only over Sales, can also edit.
Admin A has a Location Group scope of England. The England location group contains London and Manchester. Admin A can edit all of Test Category, with the exception of its operational scope.

tld-scope.statement: TLD categories take multiple operational scopes with OR logic when there is more than one, and a User-Defined custom category can be deleted only if the admin's scope exactly matches the category's scope.

quotes: You can select multiple operational scopes and when there is more than one scope, OR logic is used to find a match.
You can only delete a custom category that belongs to the User-Defined super category if your administrator scope exactly matches the scope of the custom category.

api-scopes-field.title: How the API represents a custom category's operational scope
api-scopes-field.detail: The help pages describe the operational scope options. The API, SDK and Terraform representation (a scopes field) was not read in this pass, so the mapping from the console options to fields is unstated.
